paragraphs.text: אַתָּה בְחַרְתָּנוּ מִכָּל הָעַמִּים. אָהַבְתָּ אוֹתָנוּ וְרָצִיתָ בָּנוּ. וְרוֹמַמְתָּנוּ מִכָּל הַלְּשׁוֹנוֹת. וְקִדַּשְׁתָּנוּ בְּמִצְוֹתֶיךָ. וְקֵרַבְתָּנוּ מַלְכֵּנוּ לַעֲבוֹדָתֶךָ. וְשִׁמְךָ הַגָּדוֹל וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ עָלֵינוּ קָרָאתָ:
uncertainties: בְחַרְתָּנוּ: under bet I see a shva, but I can't tell whether bet has a dagesh. There is also a small mark after ח at the patah/resh area that could be a meteg. Unresolved.
אָהַבְתָּ: there are marks under א and ה. I read them as qamats and patah, but a meteg on either can't be ruled out.
אַתָּה: I can't confirm a dagesh in ת at this scan resolution.
וְקֵרַבְתָּנוּ (end of line 2): there is a small mark next to the tsere under ק that could be a meteg. Unresolved.
הַלְּשׁוֹנוֹת, וְקִדַּשְׁתָּנוּ, בְּמִצְוֹתֶיךָ, וְרוֹמַמְתָּנוּ: I can't verify the dageshes in ל, ד, ב and the holam on the first ו at this resolution.
מִצְוֹתֶיךָ and לַעֲבוֹדָתֶךָ: final ך is printed with a qamats inside it. The holam placement on ו in מִצְוֹתֶיךָ (צְוֹ vs צְו) is unclear.

paragraphs.text: וַתִּתֶּן־לָנוּ יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ בְּאַהֲבָה אֶת־יוֹם (הַשַּׁבָּת הַזֶּה וְאֶת יוֹם) הַזִּכָּרוֹן הַזֶּה. יוֹם (זִכְרוֹן) תְּרוּעָה (בְּאַהֲבָה) מִקְרָא קֹדֶשׁ זֵכֶר לִיצִיאַת מִצְרָיִם:
uncertainties: The bracketed Sabbath insertions are printed in a smaller font. The first bracket opens at the end of line 1 (הַשַּׁבָּת הַזֶּה) and closes at the start of line 2 (וְאֶת יוֹם).
וַתִּתֶּן־לָנוּ: the maqaf is clearly printed. Under לָ the mark is qamats, and I can't tell whether a meteg is there too.
בְּאַהֲבָה (main text) and (בְּאַהֲבָה) (bracketed): I can't confirm a dagesh in ב.
הַשַּׁבָּת (small font): I can't confirm the dageshes in שׁ and ב.
קֹדֶשׁ: possible meteg next to the holam/segol region. Unresolved.
מִצְרָיִם: under ר there may be a meteg beside the qamats. Unresolved.

paragraphs.text: אתה בחרתנו Thou hast chosen us from all peoples, loved us and found delight in us and exalted us above all tongues and sanctified us through Thy commandments, and brought us near, O our King, to Thy service and proclaimed Thy great and holy Name unto us.

ותתן־לנו Thou hast given us, O Lord our God, in love this day (of the Sabbath and this day) of remembrance, a day (of remembrance) of Teruah (in love) for a sacred convoca-tion, a reminder of the exodus from Egypt.
uncertainties: "convoca-tion" is hyphenated across the line break in print, so the word is "convocation".
In the Hebrew incipit, the mark between ותתן and לנו is printed as a maqaf/hyphen.
